key_points: Berkshire disclosed a $212.38M increase in its Lennar position to nearly 10%, signaling active capital deployment by the successor regime under Greg Abel.
The Warren Buffett transition to Greg Abel as chairman appears orderly and has had a muted market reaction, reducing the long-uncertainty discount on BRK-B.
Greg Abel already controls ~$47B in investment decisions, partially resolving the key question of successor capability.
BRK-B has risen ~79% over the past 5 years, and some analysts argue it may now be near or above fair value, tempering upside.
No major change to the underlying earnings power of Berkshire's insurance, energy, and operating businesses; the thesis remains intact but with a slower compounding profile post-Buffett.
